clue.text: Mobile help line once out of order

indicators.note: something out of order is jumbled, so these letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A helpline that once served callers has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' rearranges HELP, L (line) and ONCE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile is the British name for a portable telephone carried about.

clue.text: Be deeply distressed to produce small pieces?

explanation.surface: Someone so upset they go to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being badly upset is being 'cut up' in British idiom, and chopping something into bits is also to cut it up.

clue.text: Folder could be free on part of plant

parts.note: loose means free, unattached
a leaf is a part of a plant

explanation.surface: A gardener's folder blows free across a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose-leaf binder is a folder with removable pages.

clue.text: Leading batsman goes by tube for a trial run

parts.note: a pipe is a tube
in cricket the opener is the batsman who goes in first

explanation.surface: A star cricketer travels to a match by Underground train.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opening batsman goes in first. 'tube' suggests London's Underground, but here it is just a hollow cylinder; 'goes by' puts the two words side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe-opener is a preliminary exercise or warm-up, a practice before the real event.

clue.text: The goon, funny, very active

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters are to be reordered

explanation.surface: A comic goon who is always bustling about.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the go is busy and constantly moving.

clue.text: Typical example of mine in English 'ouse

indicators.note: in places the word for mine inside the other letters

parts.note: 'ouse is house with its H dropped, so home loses its H the same way
a pit is a mine

explanation.surface: A dropped-aitch Englishman shows off his mine as a model specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ouse, the Cockney dropped-H pronunciation of house, signals 'OME, home without the H.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect specimen or embodiment of a type.

clue.text: Fast attack containing power

indicators.note: containing means the word for attack holds the other letter

parts.note: a raid is an attack

explanation.surface: A powerful, speedy assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means quick, swift.

clue.text: Makes a noise in the ranks

definitions.meaning: to row (rhyming with cow) is to quarrel noisily
lines or ranks of people or things

explanation.surface: A soldier causes a disturbance among the ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Row as a din or argument rhymes with 'cow'; as a line it rhymes with 'go': two words with one spelling.

clue.text: Old vessel captured by old man in hooded coat

indicators.note: captured by puts the vessel inside the word for old man

parts.note: pa is father, the old man
Noah's Ark is the old vessel

explanation.surface: A father seizes an ancient ship while wearing a hooded jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof jacket.

clue.text: Nominate, but not yet appointed?

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means to name or choose
... as an adjective after a title means chosen but not yet in office

explanation.surface: Someone is put forward for a post they don't yet hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A president-designate has been named for the office but has not taken it up.

clue.text: Scout group's inadequate time to make comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: poor means inadequate

explanation.surface: The Scouts' poor showing means it's time for them to fight back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make comeback' reverses POOR and T together to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a unit of Scouts.

clue.text: Tour conductors? They'll set things off

parts.note: a trip is a tour
wires conduct electricity

explanation.surface: Tour guides who trigger alarms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductors' looks like tour guides or orchestra leaders but means electrical wires.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripwires are stretched cords that activate a trap, alarm or explosive when touched.

clue.text: New portent in phone broadcast a remarkable thing

indicators.note: in puts the new omen inside the rearranged letters
broadcast means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an omen is a portent

explanation.surface: A new warning sign broadcast by phone is something extraordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scrambles the letters of the phone, and 'in' lodges the new portent inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A phenomenon is an extraordinary occurrence or marvel.

clue.text: The Scots go in an organised group

definitions.meaning: the Scots verb meaning to go
a band of people acting together

explanation.surface: Scots set off as a band.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect 'gang' means walk or go; in standard English it is a band of people.

clue.text: Outburst of many words at the dance, for a game

parts.note: a volley is a torrent of words
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone sounds off at a dance about a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Volleyball is a team sport played over a high net.

clue.text: Loosely tether ring to that

indicators.note: loosely means not fixed tightly, so the letters move about

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Tie a tether loosely to a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereto is formal language for to that matter or thing.

clue.text: Unruly Brutus mainly upset on period of fasting

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters are jumbled
mainly means most of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Brutus is badly upset during a period of fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the last S of Brutus, and 'upset' rearranges BRUTU to TURBU.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbulent means disorderly or riotous.

clue.text: Introductory parts I axed or replaced

indicators.note: replaced means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has cut and replaced the opening sections of a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Exordia (plural of exordium) are the opening sections of a discourse or treatise.

clue.text: Drunk pater's in the river, beyond hope

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: drunk means sozzled, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Father, drunk, has fallen into the river and is in a hopeless state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' scrambles the letters of pater's, and 'in' places them inside the river, the Dee in Wales and Cheshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate describes a situation so bad there is little or no hope.

clue.text: Consider on the spot mostly on time

parts.note: re means about or on, as in a memo heading

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: a fleck is a spot

explanation.surface: Think it over on the spot, and do it mostly on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final K from FLECK.
explanation.definitionFit: To reflect is to think carefully about something.

clue.text: Money drawer's mature years working on the land

parts.note: a till is a cash drawer
age means old age, mature years

explanation.surface: A cashier's drawer has reached a ripe old age down on the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the cultivation of soil for crops.

clue.text: Keyboard instrument backing part of the nonet selection

indicators.note: backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A keyboard accompanies part of a selection for nine players.
explanation.walkthrough: A nonet is a group of nine musicians. ETSELEC, from 'part of' NONET SELECTION, read back by 'backing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A celeste is a small keyboard instrument with hammers striking metal plates, heard in Tchaikovsky's Sugar Plum Fairy.

clue.text: City of student marches (termly)

indicators.note: of signals a run of letters taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: In a university city, students protest each term.
explanation.walkthrough: The city's letters run across 'marches' and 'termly'. Chester is a historic city in north-west England near the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester is an English cathedral city in Cheshire.

clue.text: Cancel a French party

parts.note: un is French for a
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Call off a French celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo is to reverse or annul something done.

clue.text: Take plant from container in the warehouse?

definitions.meaning: to ... is to remove a plant from its pot

explanation.surface: A gardener repots stock in a storage shed.
explanation.definitionFit: De-pot means unpot a plant; a depot is a store or warehouse.

clue.text: Ye sad elephant, no worker, could be an inattentive one

indicators.note: could be says the letters may be rearranged into something else

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A sad elephant that won't work might be a dozy fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no worker' removes ANT from the letters of YE SAD ELEPHANT, and 'could be' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepyhead is a drowsy or dreamy person who isn't paying attention.

clue.text: Last bit of mud on part of shoe remained

indicators.note: last bit of picks out the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the welt is the leather strip joining a shoe's upper to its sole

explanation.surface: Mud clung on to part of a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt is the past of dwell, to stay or reside.

clue.text: A reluctant grey?

parts.note: shy means reluctant, hesitant

explanation.surface: A timid, colourless person.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy means ash-coloured, a pale grey.

clue.text: English name Long embraces a ship, by the way

indicators.note: embraces means the word for long wraps around the other letters

parts.note: to pant for is to long for
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An Englishman called Long hugs a ship as he passes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like a surname but means yearn, PANT.
explanation.definitionFit: En passant is French for in passing, incidentally.

clue.text: Cognisant artist set back in wonder

indicators.note: in puts the reversed letters inside the word for wonder

parts.note: awe is wonder

indicators.note: set back means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A knowing painter, set back in amazement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' turns the Royal Academician round before it goes inside the word for wonder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognisant means having knowledge of something, informed.

clue.text: Inferior place for water drink not allowed inside

indicators.note: inside puts the teetotal letters within the river

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river, a place for water
TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: A shabby spot by the water where alcohol is banned.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay is Scotland's longest river; TT (teetotal) goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatty means shabby, worn and poor in quality.

clue.text: Register intended, we hear, to link up with odd loner

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters are rearranged
we hear says the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A lonely misfit signs up, apparently on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges LONER to ENROL, followed by MENT, which is said like MEANT ('we hear').
explanation.definitionFit: Enrolment is the act of signing on or registering.
